title: Entropy Trace findings.json
description: Canonical output schema for one sink's computed entropy-provenance chain under one build profile. This schema is frozen from this point on: report.py, sarif.py, the web UI, and CI all read this file and nothing else. A backward-incompatible change bumps schema_version's major component and adds a new $id.

schema_version.description: Semver of this schema, not of the tool. Downstream consumers should refuse to read a major version they don't recognise.

label.description: Human-readable label for this specific run (e.g. which corpus case / commit this is).

build_profile.description: The declared build configuration this chain was computed under.

target_macros.description: Repo-relative path to the data/targets/*.yaml this analysis captured its predefined-macro environment from. Absent for a profile with no ARM target (e.g. Trust Wallet Core's host-compiled CMake build, target_yaml=None).

sysroot.description: Whether a real target sysroot (compiler built-ins + newlib) was used for this analysis, or system headers resolved against the analysis host instead. `used: false` is not an error state -- it's the honest, structural fact that must never be silent, since a project with no target sysroot configured still analyses correctly, just with a real (documented) class of risk.

cache_key.description: The target YAML's own sysroot.cache_key -- the recipe, not the resolved content.

resolved_packages.description: Package name -> exact resolved version string (e.g. "newlib-arm-none-eabi-4.2.0.20211231-r1"), read from the running container at fetch time. Recorded because the source repository is rolling, so the recipe alone doesn't identify what was actually fetched.

sink.description: The entropy-critical sink this chain starts from, with its taxonomy classification.

entropy_critical.description: Fixed per category, never inferred per-instance. A finding with entropy_critical=false must never be surfaced as a failure -- RFC 6979/BIP-340 nonces, BIP-32 child derivation, BIP-85, and address/txid generation are correct constructions, not bugs.

mechanism.description: How the sink was located: a named data/sinks.yaml entry, or a structural anchor (e.g. the BIP-32 "Bitcoin seed" HMAC key literal).

config_values.description: Build-configuration values (macros etc.) that were actually read from source and that determined which branch of the analysed code is live under this profile -- the whole reason this project preprocesses instead of reading source as text.

chain.description: Every hop from the sink to the terminal, in walk order, each with file:line evidence. A chain that stops with status=UNKNOWN still reports every hop it successfully made.

kind.description: python_sink: the originating sink function. ffi: a Python-to-C boundary crossing. c_call: a plain C function call. python_call: a dotted Python call classified directly by name against the registry, with no FFI/C resolution at all.

resolution_verdict.description: Only meaningful for kind=c_call. 'local': the call target was defined in the same translation unit, no cross-TU resolution needed. 'RESOLVED': resolve.resolve() was invoked (an extern reference) and found exactly one definition across the build set -- a hop with a location attached, and the walk must continue through it, never treated as a pass on its own.

terminal.description: The classified terminal, or null if status=UNKNOWN.

matched_entry.description: The data/sources.yaml entry's `symbol` field that matched.

status.description: UNKNOWN is never silently a pass -- policy.py decides PR-mode vs audit-mode handling of it; this schema only records the fact.

unknown_reason.description: Required (non-null) when status=UNKNOWN: names exactly what was tried and why it didn't resolve, never left blank.

unknown_count.description: Number of UNKNOWN hops/edges encountered while building this finding -- the honest metric worth leading benchmark reporting with. For entropy_shape="mix", this counts every UNKNOWN contributor across the whole mix, not merely whether the head contribution happens to be unknown.

entropy_shape.description: Mirrors coverage.chains[] head entry's own entropy_shape -- see that field's description. Additive; absent on a findings.json from before this field existed.

contributions.description: Mirrors coverage.chains[] head entry's own contributions -- see that field's description.

coverage.description: Whole-tree sweep: every sink this project's two real sink-location mechanisms (the BIP-32 structural anchor, the data/sinks.yaml catalogue) find in the analysed build, each traced to a classified terminal or an honest UNKNOWN. This is the audit-tool number, not the single-chain one above -- it matters more than any individual `chain` result because it says how much of the tree was actually looked at, not just whether one named sink resolved.

chains.description: One entry per sink found, whether or not its chain closed.

notes.description: Caveats that travel with this verdict: for a mix, the sources that could not be traced (a mix with a traced good source and untraced others passes in pr mode, and says so here). Absent when there is nothing to say. Additive.

matched_entry.description: The source-list entry that classified this terminal (the `symbol` field of data/sources.yaml or of the profile's own list). Present when status is CLASSIFIED. Additive.

match_kind.description: How it matched: `function_name`, the terminal function's own name is on the list; `body_contains`, text on the list appears in its body (for example a generator named inside it). Additive.

chain.description: Same hop-list shape as the top-level `chain` field, populated for every sink in this coverage sweep -- not just the headline sink -- so a per-sink SARIF codeFlow or UI chain view can be built for any of them. Empty for a sink whose trace never started (e.g. a structural-anchor sink whose entry point is a formal parameter, not a callable).

entropy_shape.description: Whether this sink's entropy comes from exactly one traced source ("single", most sinks) or an independent combination of more than one ("mix", e.g. a function that concatenates an MCU TRNG read with a secure-element read before hashing). Additive -- absent on a findings.json from before this field existed, which every consumer must treat identically to "single" with `contributions` holding one entry matching this sink's own status/terminal_category/chain (true by construction whenever this field IS present, for a "single" sink).

contributions.description: Every independent entropy source this sink's result is built from, each walked and classified completely independently of the others (independent sources combined by XOR, concatenation-then-hash, or an equivalent mixing function take the maximum of their inputs, not the minimum -- there's no single chain to report for a mix, and no reason to force one). Always at least one entry when present. For entropy_shape="single" this is exactly a one-entry restatement of this sink's own status/terminal_category/chain/unknown_reason -- additive, not a replacement for those fields.

source_expr.description: The dotted Python attribute path or C symbol this contribution's walk started from, e.g. "ngu.random.bytes" or "callgate.read_rng".

matched_entry.description: As on the sink entry: the source-list entry that classified this contribution's terminal. Additive.

chain.description: Same hop-list shape as the top-level `chain` field, self-contained from this sink's own entry point through to this one contribution's terminal (or its own break point).

policy.description: (entropy_critical, terminal classification, mode) -> verdict, computed over every entropy_critical sink in `coverage.chains`. This is the pass/fail decision every other consumer (SARIF, the GitHub Action's exit code, the HTML report, the web UI) reads -- none of them re-derive a verdict from raw categories themselves. A PASS here means only that the sink resolved, under this policy mode, to a source class this policy accepts -- never that the resulting keys are secure or safe.

verdicts.description: One entry per entropy_critical sink in `coverage.chains` -- sinks with entropy_critical=false are never evaluated and do not appear here. Neither does a sink found by the BIP-32 structural anchor whose chain could not be traced (mechanism=structural_anchor, status=UNKNOWN): it marks where a seed is consumed, cannot resolve yet, and takes no part in the verdict. If every sink found is such an anchor, overall_verdict is that of a bare UNKNOWN (WARN in pr mode, FAIL in audit mode), never PASS.

overall_verdict.description: The worst (FAIL > WARN > PASS) verdict among `verdicts` -- what the GitHub Action's exit code is based on.
